answer: Each agent must keep a live lantern: a sequential Merkle chain of state hashes sampled from the shared river of recent consensus epochs. Every epoch it publishes a new segment committing to the prior lantern plus the current dune of network fees. An attacker running N fakes pays N times the continuous hashing and bandwidth cost; missing one lantern kills the chain and requires a full dune-rebuild deposit, rendering mass cloning far costlier than honest single-identity work.
